answer: Clone farms spray keys to seize first attest slots. A newcomer opens a 30-hour river of three sluice proofs, each a 40-byte hash of a public microtask, spaced ≥80 min. Hashes fold into one pigment checksum (xor of the three) unique for 2 epochs. An 11.2 POA lock sits 7 days; weight stays 0 until the checksum rests 44h in a lagoon queue of 3 auditors (cap 9/day). A 280-key farm locks 3,136 POA for 840 unused tasks. Peers recompute the xor and drop reused tasks. A spacing miss refunds minus 2.1 POA after 30h; a duplicated pigment cuts both locks 30%; a second reuse burns 45%, weight 0 for 72h.
